claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform fine-lamellar microstructure.
The starting alloy has limited strength and plasticity for the intended application.
The starting alloy has inadequate creep and corrosion resistance under the proposed extreme service conditions.
The proposed intervention is aging at approximately 600°C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere, followed by rapid quenching.
The proposed aging treatment will form coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates in the FCC lamellae.
The L12 precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the FCC lamellae.
Formation of the L12 precipitates will refine phase boundaries and improve interfacial coherency.
The L12 nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion through Orowan bowing.
Precipitation-induced obstruction of dislocations will increase yield strength.
Precipitation-induced obstruction of dislocations will increase work hardening.
Coherent L12 precipitates will stabilize phase boundaries and reduce interlamellar failure during cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Maintaining interfacial integrity will mitigate localized corrosion.
The treatment will increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength by approximately 15–20% relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
The treatment will improve room-temperature creep resistance.
The treatment will improve resistance to high-temperature deformation.
The treatment will improve corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
The strength, creep, and corrosion improvements will be achieved without compromising ductility.
The treatment will be effective from room temperature to 700°C, provided that the designed microstructural scale is maintained and over-aging is avoided.
The magnitude of property enhancement and uniformity of L12 precipitation depend on aging temperature, aging time, and cooling rate.
